Health Monitoring System
A Health Monitoring System is a technology used to continuously observe, measure and record a person's health conditions. It helps detect health problems at an early stage and allows doctors to provide timely treatment. It monitors important health parameters such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, oxygen levels, breathing rate and sleep patterns.
The system works with the help of special sensors and wearable devices that collect information from the human body. This information is then transferred to a computer or monitoring device, where it can be analysed. If any unusual changes are detected, an alert can be generated so that medical attention can be provided.
Health Monitoring Systems are especially important for astronauts during space missions. In space, conditions such as microgravity, radiation and isolation can affect the human body. Astronauts wear special devices that monitor their vital signs and send health-related information to doctors on Earth. This helps scientists understand how space travel affects the human body and take necessary precautions.
In conclusion, Health Monitoring Systems play an important role in modern healthcare and space exploration. They help protect human health, improve safety and ensure that medical problems are identified and treated at the right time.
